Definition: Asherah (or Astarte) a Phoenician goddess; also an image of the same
BiblicalUsage: Asherah is the goddess of the Canaanites, and the grove that bears her name, and the Bible names her wherever Israel goes wrong. Judah builds high places and images and groves under every green tree, Asa removes his mother Maachah from being queen because she made an idol in a grove, and Gideon is told to throw down the altar of Baal and cut down the grove that is by it.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Asherah is the proof that idolatry in Israel was not a foreign import but a home-grown sin: the groves stand under every green tree, a queen mother makes the idol, and it takes a king and a judge to cut them down. And I hold that the groves are still cut down the same way, by men who will obey God at night with ten men and a new altar.
